source_text: Ecce officium liberae voluntatis: Si, inquit, mundaverit quis semetipsum a societate vasorum vilium (quo nomine vitia denotantur), erit vas in honorem sanctificatum, utile Domino, ad omne opus bonum paratum [n364] . Haec igitur vasa, studiis propriis, aut ad iram, aut ad gloriam praeparantur; Deus autem notam facit potentiam suam in utroque, vel severitatem in impios exserendo, vel benedictionem fidelibus largiendo. Apparuit itaque hanc sententiam egregii praeceptoris, nec Manichaeis opem sensibus attulisse, et e diverso nos consequenter armasse.
pass_a_gloss: See the office of free will: If, he says, anyone shall have cleansed himself from the society of cheap vessels (by which name vices are denoted), he will be a vessel unto honor sanctified, useful to the Lord, prepared unto every good work. These vessels therefore, by their own studies, are prepared either unto wrath, or unto glory; but God makes his power known in each, either by putting forth severity in the impious, or by lavishing blessing on the faithful. It has appeared therefore that this sentence of the outstanding teacher, neither brought help to Manichaean senses, and from the other side has consequently armed us.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: See the task of free will: “If anyone cleanses himself” from association with cheap vessels, a name that denotes vices, “he will be a vessel sanctified for honor, useful to the Lord, prepared for every good work” (2 Timothy 2:21). These vessels are therefore prepared for either wrath or glory through their own pursuits. God makes his power known in both cases, either by displaying severity toward the impious or by bestowing blessing on the faithful. It is therefore clear that this statement of the outstanding teacher has given no aid to Manichaean views; on the contrary, it has consistently armed us.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
